taxes.name: NYC sales tax on food and drinks
taxes.appliesIf: coffee and tea served in a cup, food eaten in the shop, heated food and sandwiches

vendorCredit.condition: quarterly return filed and paid in full on time

taxes.note: CORRECTION of the existing row (same rate, new calendar). NYS Tax Bulletin TB-ST-275: a new vendor files quarterly; the sales tax quarters end on the last day of February, May, August and November, and the return is due 20 days later: March 20, June 20, September 20, December 20 - not in the month after a calendar quarter. $300,000 or more of taxable receipts in a quarter moves the shop to monthly filing; back to quarterly only after four quarters below it. TB-ST-925: a quarterly filer who files and pays on time keeps 5% of the tax, at most $200 a quarter. At $51,000 a month the return is 3 x $51,000 x 8.875% = $13,579.

taxes.name: Commuter transportation tax on the owner's own earnings (MCTMT, self-employed)
taxes.appliesIf: only when the owner's net self-employment earnings in New York City are more than $150,000 a year
taxes.note: Form IT-2105 instructions for 2026: 0.60% of net self-employment earnings allocated to Zone 1 (New York City) when they exceed $150,000; the threshold was $50,000 for 2025 and earlier and is tested per person, even on a joint return. Paid with the owner's estimated tax. Game rate 0: the reference shop earns its owner about $117,000. At $160,000 the bill would be $960 a year. Separate from the employer MCTMT in _common (payroll over $312,500 a quarter).

taxes.name: NYC General Corporation Tax (only if you elect S corporation status)
taxes.appliesIf: only for a business taxed as an S corporation
taxes.note: NYC Department of Finance: the city has no S corporation election and does not recognize the state one; a federal S corporation pays General Corporation Tax of 8.85% on income computed as if it were a C corporation. The default single-member LLC pays the 4% Unincorporated Business Tax instead (nyc_ubt in _common). Game rate 0; it switches on with the tax_structure lever. See extra.mechanics.tax_structure_s_corp.

taxes.name: NYS S corporation fixed dollar minimum tax
taxes.appliesIf: only for a business taxed as an S corporation
taxes.note: Form CT-3-S instructions: a New York S corporation pays a fixed dollar minimum by New York receipts: $25 up to $100,000, $50 up to $250,000, $175 up to $500,000, $300 up to $1 million, $1,000 up to $5 million. A cafe with $612,000 of sales pays $300 a year. Game rate 0 unless the S corporation option is chosen.

taxes.name: NYS biennial statement fee
taxes.note: NYS Department of State: an LLC files a biennial statement every two years; the fee is $9. Game amount: $9 / 2 = $4.50 a year. Trivial money, but an unfiled statement shows the company as past due in the state database, which lenders and buyers check.

taxes.name: NY use tax on purchases bought without sales tax
taxes.appliesIf: equipment, furniture or supplies bought out of state or online when the seller did not charge New York sales tax
taxes.note: Tax Bulletin TB-ST-910: a business that buys equipment or supplies without paying New York tax owes use tax on the cost, shipping included, and reports it on its sales tax return; tax paid to another state is credited. In New York City the rate is the same 8.875%. The pack already budgets this inside the setup item equipment_delivery_tax, so the recurring game rate is 0. A $7,600 espresso machine bought tax-free out of state still owes $674.50.

taxes.name: Sales tax when you sell your equipment or your business
taxes.appliesIf: only when you sell furniture and equipment, at closing or as part of selling the business
taxes.note: NYS Tax: a business that sells its assets must collect the sales tax due on them, give the buyer Form TP-153, and pay the tax with a final return due within 20 days. Furniture and equipment are taxed at 8.875% of their allocated price; inventory for resale and goodwill are not (the split is my reading of the bulk sale rules, not quoted from the page). On $40,000 of equipment the buyer pays $3,550 on top of the price. Used by extra.mechanics.exit_sale.

taxes.name: Paid Family Leave contribution (withheld from workers)
taxes.appliesIf: every employer withholds it from each worker's pay
taxes.note: paidfamilyleave.ny.gov and NYS DFS: in 2026 workers pay 0.432% of wages, at most $411.91 a year; in 2027 0.452%, at most $451.81. The employer pays nothing but must withhold and pass it on to the insurer, so the game rate is 0. It is one more line on every pay stub and one more balance that is not the owner's money.

taxes.name: Income tax on the gain when you sell the business
taxes.appliesIf: only in the year you sell the business or its assets
taxes.note: IRS closing-a-business checklist: the sale is reported on Form 8594 (price split by asset class) and Form 4797. Equipment that was written off (section 179 or 100% bonus depreciation, IRS Publication 946) comes back as ordinary income when sold; goodwill held over a year is a long-term capital gain (federal 0% or 15% for this owner). New York State and City tax every gain as ordinary income, and UBT applies to the gain too. My blended planning rate for the exit mechanic: 28% of the gain (federal 12-22% ordinary on recaptured equipment or 15% on goodwill, state 5.4%, city 3.876%, UBT up to 4%). Not a quote; an accountant computes it from the allocation.

taxes.name: Income tax on debt a lender forgives
taxes.appliesIf: only when a lender settles or writes off a debt you owe
taxes.note: IRS Publication 4681: a canceled debt is ordinary income, reported to the IRS on Form 1099-C, unless the borrower was insolvent just before the cancellation (excluded up to the amount of insolvency, Form 982) or the debt was discharged in bankruptcy. Game rate 0; the exit mechanic adds the forgiven amount to taxable income when the owner still has more assets than debts.

taxes.name: NYS and NYC pass-through entity tax (optional)
taxes.appliesIf: only partnerships and S corporations that elect it; a single-member LLC taxed on the owner's return cannot
taxes.note: NYS Tax: the elective pass-through entity tax is 6.85% of income up to $2 million; the New York City version is a flat 3.876%. The owners get a matching credit on their personal returns, so the point is a federal deduction, not a lower state bill. Open only to partnerships and S corporations. Game rate 0: the pack's owner is a single-member LLC.

monthlyCosts.name: Business owner's policy: liability, property, interruption
monthlyCosts.note: CORRECTION of the note, amount unchanged. Seen at Insureon (page updated autumn 2026): coffee shops pay on average $126 a month ($1,507 a year) for a business owner's policy, $82 a month for general liability alone, $88 a month for workers' compensation. These are US averages of one broker's small customers; the New York City reserve of $250 stays. Two things the old note missed: the liability part is priced on sales and trued up by a premium audit after the policy year (extra.mechanics.insurance_claims_and_audit), and business insurance for New York-area service firms rose 7% in the last year (Manhattan Chamber of Commerce, reported by Bloomberg and Insurance Journal, October 2026).

monthlyCosts.name: Business checking account and cash deposit fees
monthlyCosts.note: Secondary sources on Chase Business Complete Checking, 2026: $15 a month, waived with a $2,000 minimum daily balance; the first $5,000 of cash deposits per statement cycle is free, then about $2.50-$3 per $1,000 (sources differ; the bank's own fee schedule was not readable). A shop with 10% of $51,000 in cash deposits about $5,100 a month, right at the limit. Planning value: $15 fee in thin months plus a few dollars of deposit and change-order fees = $20.

monthlyCosts.name: Refunds and card disputes
monthlyCosts.note: Seen at Square: a disputed amount is held at once, the seller has 7 days to answer, the bank may take up to 90 days, there is no dispute fee, and the processing fee is not returned when the customer wins. No public statistic of dispute or refund rates for coffee shops was found; tap-and-go disputes are rare. Planning value: 0.1% of sales ($51 a month at $51,000), mostly refunded remakes and double charges.

monthlyCosts.name: SBA 7(a) loan payment (per $100,000 borrowed)
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. Seen at SBA: the maximum rate on a $50,001-$250,000 loan is the base rate + 6.0%; working capital and equipment loans run up to 10 years. With the Wall Street Journal prime rate at 7.00% (unchanged since September 16, 2026) the cap is 13.0%. Level payment on $100,000 over 120 months at 13%: $1,493 a month, $79,200 of interest over the life. Most 7(a) loans are variable: each quarter point of prime moves the payment by about $14.

monthlyCosts.name: SBA microloan payment (on $50,000)
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. Seen at SBA: microloans go up to $50,000 (the average is about $13,000), interest is generally 8%-13%, and the program rules give six years to repay (some 2026 SBA articles say seven). Level payment on $50,000 at 10.5%, the middle of the range, over 72 months: $939. Lent by nonprofit intermediaries; since April 1, 2026 the borrower must be a U.S. citizen or national.

monthlyCosts.name: Family loan payment (on $50,000 at the IRS minimum rate)
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. IRS Rev. Rul. 2026-21: the short-term applicable federal rate for November 2026 is 4.67% (4.25% in October); the October mid-term rate (loans of 3 to 9 years) was 4.61%, the November mid-term figure was not seen. A family loan above $10,000 at less than this rate is treated as a gift of the missing interest. $50,000 over 60 months at 4.61%: $935 a month.

monthlyCosts.name: Merchant cash advance: share of card sales taken every day
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. Trade and broker sources, 2026: factor rates 1.15-1.50 (restaurants: $30,000-$80,000 at 1.25-1.35) and a holdback of 5%-25% of card sales. Game product: $40,000 advanced for $54,000 (factor 1.35), holdback 15% of card sales x 90% of sales on cards = 13.5% of sales. At $51,000 a month that is $6,885 a month for 7.8 months: about 88% a year (monthly rate 7.3%). The row ends when $54,000 has been collected. Many funders take a fixed daily bank debit instead, which does not fall when sales fall.

monthlyCosts.name: Interest on a business credit card balance (per $10,000 carried)
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. NerdWallet, November 2026: large issuers' business cards charge roughly 16.99%-28.74% after a 0% introductory period (often 12 months); Curinos put the bank average for rewards business cards near 16.5% in July 2026. Planning rate 21%: $10,000 x 21% / 12 = $175 a month of interest, with nothing repaid. Business cards are personally guaranteed.

monthlyCosts.name: Equipment lease payment (on $25,000 of equipment)
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. No public rate sheet for restaurant equipment leases was found; lessors quote case by case. Planning value: $25,000 over 60 months at 12% = $556 a month ($33,360 in all). The lease is usually personally guaranteed and is owed in full even if the shop closes; the equipment goes back to the lessor. Source cited only for context: the Fed's 2026 small business credit survey, where 60% of borrowers from online lenders found the real cost higher than expected.

monthlyCosts.name: NYC Future Fund loan: monthly interest (per $50,000)
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. NYC Business, 2026 terms: loans of $25,000-$500,000 at 7.5% for up to five years, 3% origination fee, no application fee; interest is paid monthly and principal is due only in months when revenue passes a set threshold; personal guaranty from owners of 20% or more and a UCC filing. Needs at least 12 months in business, one filed tax return and $50,000 of yearly revenue, so it cannot fund an opening. $50,000 x 7.5% / 12 = $312.50.

monthlyCosts.name: Owner's own health insurance (marketplace silver plan, one adult)
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. NY State of Health table for 2026: the lowest cost silver plan is $806.61 a month in Bronx, Kings and Queens counties ($828.79 in 2025). The table does not label the tier; I read it as one adult, which is how the marketplace quotes its county benchmarks. Before subsidies. A personal cost, not a business expense on the profit-and-loss statement, but it comes out of the same pocket the month the owner leaves a job with benefits.

monthlyCosts.name: Cyber liability insurance
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. Seen at Insureon: food and beverage businesses pay about $129 a month for cyber coverage. It pays for a card data breach or a locked register; a business owner's policy does not.

monthlyCosts.name: Employment practices liability insurance
monthlyCosts.note: CONDITIONAL ROW: charge it only while the option in activeWhen is on; a plain merge must not add it to every shop. Seen at Insureon: the average is $257 a month across its small-business customers (38% pay under $200), with an average deductible of $10,000. It answers discrimination, harassment and wrongful firing claims. Unpaid wage claims are usually excluded or capped at a small defense-cost sublimit (general industry practice; the page does not say so), so it does not rescue a labor shortcut.

setup.name: SBA loan upfront guaranty fee (per $100,000 borrowed)
setup.note: SBA Information Notice 5000-881797 (fees for loans approved October 1, 2026 - September 30, 2027), read through the lender association's summary because the notice text was not readable: 2% of the guaranteed portion on loans of $150,000 or less, 3% on $150,001-$700,000, 3.5% above that; 0.25% when the loan runs 12 months or less. SBA guarantees 85% of loans up to $150,000 (seen at sba.gov), and lenders pass the fee on: $100,000 x 85% x 2% = $1,700. The 0.55% yearly servicing fee may not be charged to the borrower.

setup.name: Con Edison security deposit for a new business account
setup.note: Con Edison, rights of nonresidential customers: a deposit may not be more than two times the average monthly bill (or twice the average peak-season bill when use swings widely) and is refunded when the account is closed with nothing owed. The pack models electricity at $693-$1,155 a month: 2 x $900 = $1,800. The existing item insurance_utility_deposits ($1,500) lumps this with the first insurance premiums and is too small to hold both. Not marked required only so that the kits stay valid; most new commercial accounts are asked for it.

setup.name: Sales tax Certificate of Authority
setup.agency: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance
setup.note: Free; apply at least 20 days before the first taxable sale (existing _common roadmap step sales_tax_certificate). Added here as a setup item so that opening without it leaves a trail. Marked not required only so that the kits stay valid: the lead should add it to the kits and set required to true. The penalty for selling without it is taken from the existing pack; the penalty page opened this session showed only the $50 penalty for not displaying it.

levers.name: Insurance beyond the basic policy

options.label: Business owner's policy only: what the lease demands
Add equipment breakdown, spoilage and sewer backup cover
Add employment practices and cyber cover as well

levers.note: $431 = $45 + $257 employment practices + $129 cyber (both seen at Insureon). The $45 for the three endorsements is a planning value with no public price behind it: insurers quote them case by case. What each option covers is in the covers list of event ids; nothing here covers a flood (separate federal flood policy) or unpaid wages.

levers.name: Card fees: who pays

options.label: Absorb card fees in your prices
Post two prices: cash, and card about 3% higher

levers.note: NYS Department of State guidance on General Business Law §518 (in force since February 11, 2024): a seller may pass on its actual card cost only if the higher card price is posted in dollars before the sale; posting a cash price and a card price is allowed. The demand effect of -2% is a game-balance value: no measurement was found. The revenue effect is 3% on the 90% of sales paid by card = 2.7% of sales, which roughly cancels the 4.1% card cost on an $8.50 ticket. Sales tax is charged on the higher price.

levers.name: Card payouts

options.label: Free next-business-day transfers
Instant transfers, 1.95% of every dollar moved

levers.note: Seen at Square: standard transfers are free and arrive the next business day for sales taken before 5 PM Pacific; none are sent on Saturday, so Friday-Sunday sales land on Monday, or Tuesday when Monday is a bank holiday. Instant and same-day transfers cost 1.95% of the amount. If every card dollar is moved instantly: 1.95% x ($51,000 x 90% x 1.08875 + $2,000 of card tips) = $1,010 a month. The honest use is a few transfers a year, about $20 per $1,000 moved.

levers.name: Sales tax and payroll tax money

options.label: Sweep tax money into a separate account every day
Leave it in the operating account

levers.note: No cost either way. With one account the bank balance looks $13,600 richer just before each sales tax date (3 x $51,000 x 8.875%) and the payroll taxes withheld for the month sit there too. The engine should show "cash that is yours" separately when the first option is on, and only the raw balance when the second is on. Spending the money and not paying is the shortcut keep_sales_tax or spend_payroll_withholding.

levers.name: Owner's estimated income tax

options.label: Pay every quarter: April 15, June 15, September 15, January 15
Keep the cash in the shop and pay it all next April, with interest

levers.note: IRS, fourth quarter of 2026: the underpayment rate is 7% a year, compounded daily. Paying late is not a violation: the IRS adds interest for the days each instalment was short. No interest at all is due if the instalments cover 100% of last year's tax (110% when last year's income was over $150,000), which a first-year owner who was an employee last year often already meets through a spouse's or own withholding. Planning cost: the reference owner owes $36,300 a year (extra.referenceMonth: $3,026 a month); each instalment is on average about 7.5 months late: $36,300 x 7% x 7.5 / 12 = $1,590 a year = $130 a month. New York State charges its own interest on its part; the state rate was not found. The real risk is not the interest: it is arriving in April without the money.

levers.name: Owner's health insurance

options.label: Stay on a spouse's employer plan
Marketplace silver plan for yourself
Marketplace silver plan for a family of four

levers.note: $806.61 is the 2026 lowest cost silver plan in Bronx, Kings and Queens counties (NY State of Health). The family figure is that premium x 2.85, the family tier factor I remember for New York's community-rated market; the factor was not verified this session. Before subsidies: for 2026 a family of four with income of $112,525-$128,600 qualifies only for reduced cost sharing (seen in the marketplace's 2026 plan card). Health insurance for New York-area service firms rose 12.9% in a year (Manhattan Chamber of Commerce, October 2026).

levers.name: How the business is taxed

options.label: Single-member LLC taxed on the owner's return
Elect S corporation status and put yourself on payroll

levers.note: The $250 a month is a planning value for the owner's own payroll run, a second set of returns and the $300 state minimum tax; no public price list. In most of the country the election saves several thousand dollars of self-employment tax. In New York City it swaps the 4% Unincorporated Business Tax (zero for profit under about $100,000) for the 8.85% General Corporation Tax. Worked example in extra.mechanics.tax_structure_s_corp: at $116,600 of profit the saving is about $3,050 a year before the extra fees and about nothing after them.

levers.name: Loan interest (only if you borrowed)

options.label: Variable: prime + 6%, moves when the Fed moves
Fixed for the whole term

levers.note: Seen at SBA: 7(a) rates are negotiated with the lender, fixed or variable, under SBA maximums pegged to the prime rate. NerdWallet's 2026 table of the fixed-rate caps (15% for $25,000 or less, down to 12% above $250,000) puts a $100,000 fixed loan at the same 13% ceiling as a variable one while prime is 7%. No cost difference at signing; the variable loan follows the event prime_rate_change. Most lenders offer variable.

levers.name: When cash is short: who waits

options.label: Pay everyone on the due date
Pay rent on the 10th and take the late fee
options.consequence: after three late months in a row the landlord sends a default notice; under a good guy guarantee the owner is then no longer a "good guy"

options.label: Stretch supplier invoices by two weeks
options.consequence: after two stretched months the roaster and the dairy move the account to cash on delivery

levers.note: Both are legal and both are what owners actually do first. The late fee is a planning value: 5% of a $6,000 rent, a common clause in New York shop leases (not a statute; read the lease). Stretching suppliers frees about two weeks of purchases once, roughly $6,600 at the reference cost of goods of $13,260 a month, and costs the open account. Neither is allowed for tax money or wages: those are the shortcuts.

shortcuts.name: Use the withheld payroll taxes to pay the rent
shortcuts.what: You run payroll properly but do not send the IRS and the state what you withheld: about 23% of payroll stays in the bank. That money is held in trust. The IRS adds 2%-15% and can charge the whole amount to you personally, LLC or not.

shortcuts.name: Add a card fee at the register
shortcuts.what: A 3% "card fee" line appears on the receipt, on debit cards too, with no card price posted: about 2.7% of sales. New York allows a surcharge only when the card price is posted before the sale and does not exceed your real cost: up to $500 per violation.

shortcuts.name: Add a 4% "wellness fee" to every check
shortcuts.what: Menu prices stay the same and a 4% fee line is added at the end. New York City restaurants may not add a surcharge on top of listed prices; a real service charge must be disclosed before the customer orders. Inspectors check receipts against the menu.

shortcuts.name: Ring lattes up as tax-free groceries
shortcuts.what: The register is set so a tenth of taxable drinks ring as exempt "beans to go": you keep 8.875% on those sales, about 0.9% of all sales. An auditor rebuilds your sales from cups and milk bought: tax back, up to 30% penalty, interest.

shortcuts.name: Pay baristas every two weeks instead of every week
shortcuts.what: Half the payroll runs and a week of wages stays in your account a little longer: about $30 a month. Baristas are manual workers and must be paid weekly. A first finding costs interest; a repeat costs damages equal to all the wages paid late.

shortcuts.name: Tell the workers' comp insurer half your payroll
shortcuts.what: Premium is charged per $100 of payroll, so reporting half of it halves the bill: about 1% of payroll. The yearly premium audit asks for your payroll tax returns. Concealing payroll counts as having no coverage: up to $2,000 per 10 days.

shortcuts.name: Take register shortages out of staff pay
shortcuts.what: When the drawer is short or a customer walks out, the barista on shift covers it: about $13 per worker a month. New York forbids deducting shortages, breakage or spoilage from wages, even when one person had the drawer. Owed back double.

shortcuts.name: Skip the disability and Paid Family Leave policy
shortcuts.what: No policy, no paperwork: saves about $3 per worker a month. It is mandatory from the first employee: a misdemeanor, a penalty of up to 0.5% of payroll plus $500, and you pay any claim yourself or 1% of payroll, whichever is more.

violations.name: Withheld payroll taxes not deposited
violations.criminal: Willfully failing to collect or pay over withheld tax is a federal felony: up to 5 years in prison and a $10,000 fine (26 U.S.C. §7202).
violations.note: IRS: the failure-to-deposit penalty is 2% for deposits 1-5 days late, 5% for 6-15 days, 10% for more than 15 days and 15% once a notice has gone unanswered for 10 days; the tiers do not stack. Game formula: the tax back plus the 15% top tier (1.15 x what was kept); interest at 7% runs on top. The Trust Fund Recovery Penalty (§6672, already cited in _common) makes the owner personally liable for 100% of the withheld part, and that debt survives bankruptcy. The filing itself is on time, so nothing looks wrong from outside until the IRS matches Form 941 against deposits: found by audit only.

violations.name: Card surcharge not posted or above the real cost
violations.note: General Business Law §518 as shown on the NY Senate site: a seller who violates the section is liable for a civil penalty of not more than $500 for each violation. The 2023 amendment (in force February 11, 2024; Department of State guide): the total card price, surcharge included, must be posted clearly before the sale, and the surcharge may not exceed what the card company charges the business. Enforced by the Attorney General and by local consumer affairs offices (in the city: DCWP). Card network rules bar surcharging debit cards (not opened this session). The game charges $500 each time it is found.

violations.name: Surcharge added on top of menu prices
violations.law: Rules of the City of New York, title 6, §5-59; NYC Administrative Code §20-700
violations.note: NYC DCWP inspection checklist: a restaurant may not add a surcharge to listed food and drink prices (its examples: a 5% living wage fee, a 20% administrative charge); a bona fide service charge is allowed only if conspicuously disclosed before food is ordered (a minimum per person, a plate-splitting charge, a mandatory tip for parties of eight or more). The fine was not on the pages opened; $350-$500 is the range of the city's consumer protection penalties as I know them, so the amounts are an estimate. A fee that reads like a tip also belongs to the staff under Labor Law §196-d.

violations.name: Taxable sales rung up as exempt
violations.criminal: Done on purpose it is the same crime as hiding sales: more than $3,000 of tax evaded within a year is a class E felony (Tax Law §1803).
violations.note: NYS Tax penalty bulletin: unpaid tax carries 10% for the first month and 1% for each month after, up to 30%, and never less than $50; interest is compounded daily. Game formula: the tax back plus the 30% maximum (1.3 x what was kept). Tax Bulletin TB-ST-806: a toasted bagel with cream cheese and an iced coffee are taxable even to go; a dozen plain bagels to go and a bag of unheated beans are not. When records are poor the state may rebuild sales with a one-day observation of the register and apply the result to three years.

violations.name: Manual workers paid less often than weekly
violations.note: Labor Law §191 requires weekly pay for manual workers (more than 25% of working time in physical labor; courts have treated food counter staff that way). The May 2025 amendment to §198(1-a), as described by Mayer Brown and other firms: an employer that paid at least twice a month owes only interest on the late wages the first time; with a prior finding it owes liquidated damages equal to 100% of the wages paid late. Game formula for a first finding: $300 of costs plus interest on one week of wages a month ($13,440 / 4.33 x 16% / 52 = about $10 a month; the 16% rate is the statutory rate as I know it, not opened). A repeat finding should charge half the payroll of the whole period: the engine needs a "second finding" flag.

violations.name: Payroll concealed from the workers' compensation insurer
violations.note: NYS Workers' Compensation Board, 2026 conference material: an employer that intentionally and materially understates or conceals payroll, or misrepresents information used to calculate the premium, is deemed to have failed to secure compensation; the civil penalty is up to $2,000 for each 10-day period or up to twice the cost of compensation for the payroll in that period. Game formula follows the existing no_wc_insurance row: $6,000 a month plus twice the premium avoided. The insurer's own premium audit bills the missing premium first.

violations.name: Shortages and breakage deducted from wages
violations.note: NYS Department of Labor: deductions for breakage, cash shortages, fines and losses to the business are illegal, and so is making the worker pay them in a separate transaction. Labor Law §198(1-a) (already in the pack): the money back plus 100% liquidated damages, interest and fees, up to six years back. Game formula: 2.0 x what was deducted. Saving estimate: register shortages of 0.1% of $51,000 = $51 a month across four baristas.

violations.name: No disability and Paid Family Leave coverage
violations.criminal: A misdemeanor: a fine of $100-$500 or up to one year in jail, or both; more for a repeat within five years (WCL §220(1)).
violations.note: NYS Workers' Compensation Board: the Board imposes up to 0.5% of the payroll for the period without coverage plus up to $500; the employer is also liable for the claims paid during that period or 1% of that payroll, whichever is greater. Game formula: $500 plus 0.5% of payroll for the months without a policy (the format has no payroll-based fine: field pctOfPayroll). The saving is tiny: the pack prices the employer's share at $17.68 per worker a year plus a little administration.

violations.name: Selling before the sales tax Certificate of Authority
violations.note: Amounts are those quoted in the existing _common roadmap step (from the DTF-17 instructions): up to $500 for the first day of business without a certificate and up to $200 for each day after, at most $10,000. The penalty bulletin opened this session lists only the $50 penalty for not displaying the certificate, so the row is an estimate. $200 x 30 days = $6,000 a month, capped at $10,000.

officials.name: IRS revenue officer
officials.realProcess: The IRS matches each quarterly Form 941 against the deposits it received. A revenue officer visits, interviews the owner (Form 4180) to decide who was responsible, and proposes the Trust Fund Recovery Penalty against that person. Liens and levies follow if nothing is paid.

reports.name: Report a surprise fee on the check (311 / Attorney General)
reports.text: In real life: a 311 complaint to the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, or a complaint to the Attorney General. An inspector compares the menu, the posted prices and a receipt. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report payroll taxes or insurance not being paid
reports.text: In real life: IRS Form 3949-A, or a fraud referral to the Workers' Compensation Board. Deposits are matched against payroll returns and the insurer audits the payroll. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

events.name: Insurance renewal: premiums up 7%
events.text: Insurers raise rates across the city. Your business policy renews at a higher price for the next twelve months.
events.note: Manhattan Chamber of Commerce figures reported by Bloomberg and Insurance Journal on October 14, 2026: over the last year business insurance for New York-area service firms rose 7%, employee health insurance 12.9%, utilities 8.5%, wages 3.4%. One bar owner's liability premium grew fivefold in four years to $24,000. Applied as the citywide average.

events.name: Workers' compensation rates fall
events.text: The state approves lower workers' compensation loss costs from October 1. Your premium drops at the next renewal.
events.note: NYS Department of Financial Services, July 15, 2026: a 21.9% decrease in the overall loss cost level from October 1, 2026, after 13.2% the year before. Each insurer multiplies the loss cost by its own filed factor, so an employer's premium falls by less: game value -15%.

events.name: Prime rate up a quarter point
events.text: Banks raise the prime rate. Variable-rate loans, credit lines and cards cost more from next month.
events.note: The Wall Street Journal prime rate was 6.75% in spring 2026 and has been 7.00% since September 16, 2026 (Bankrate and rate trackers, November 2026). A quarter point on a 13% SBA loan is 13.25 / 13 = x1.02: about $14 a month per $100,000 borrowed.

events.name: Card processor adds 5 cents per tap
events.text: Your processor changes its pricing. On small tickets the cents matter more than the percentage.
events.note: Square says its in-person rate moved to 2.6% + 15 cents on February 25, 2025; the earlier per-tap fee was 10 cents (from memory). On an $8.50 order that takes the fee from about 32 cents to 37 cents. The pack already uses 15 cents; the event is a template for the next change.

events.name: Minimum wage may rise to $17.60 on March 1
events.text: The wage floor stayed at $17.00 on January 1. The Governor has proposed $17.60 from March 1, 2027; it needs a vote in Albany.
events.note: NYS Governor's page: on January 1, 2027 the minimum wage stays at $17.00 in New York City because one of the law's off-ramp conditions was met; the Governor proposed inflation-based increases from March 1, 2027: $17.60 downstate, subject to legislation. 17.60 / 17.00 = 1.035. The pack pays $21, so the direct effect is on new hires and on the wage ladder; apply only if the bill passes.

ruleCards.title: Sales tax dates
ruleCards.text: New York's sales tax quarters end in February, May, August and November, and the return is due on the 20th of March, June, September and December. A shop taking $51,000 a month owes about $13,600 each time.

ruleCards.title: A reward for filing on time
ruleCards.text: File and pay your quarterly sales tax return on time and New York lets you keep 5% of the tax, up to $200 a quarter. File one day late and the credit is gone, replaced by a penalty of at least $50.

ruleCards.title: An LLC does not shield sales tax
ruleCards.text: Every member of an LLC can be held personally liable for 100% of the sales tax the business owes (NY Tax Law §§1131, 1133). The debt follows you after the shop closes, and bankruptcy does not erase tax you collected.

ruleCards.title: When tax goes unpaid
ruleCards.text: New York files a tax warrant, then levies bank accounts and can take up to 10% of your wages. At $10,000 of past-due tax it can suspend your driver's license after a 60-day notice. In June 2026 it seized a Manhattan restaurant.

ruleCards.title: Payroll taxes are held in trust
ruleCards.text: Taxes withheld from pay in one month are due at the IRS by the 15th of the next. Late deposits cost 2% to 15%. Use the money for rent and the IRS can bill 100% of the withheld tax to you personally (Trust Fund Recovery Penalty).

ruleCards.title: Money spent before opening
ruleCards.text: Costs before opening day are not a normal deduction. You may deduct $5,000 in year one, less every dollar over $50,000 (nothing at $55,000), and the rest over 180 months. Pre-opening rent and wages count; equipment is depreciated.

ruleCards.title: Nobody withholds tax for an owner
ruleCards.text: Estimated income tax is due April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15. Pay at least 100% of last year's tax (110% if income was over $150,000) and there is no penalty; otherwise the IRS charges 7% a year on what was short.

ruleCards.title: The IRS already knows your card sales
ruleCards.text: Your card processor reports every dollar of card sales on Form 1099-K, with no minimum. An auditor starts from that number and can estimate cash sales by watching your register for one day and applying the ratio to three years.

ruleCards.title: Card money arrives later
ruleCards.text: Square pays out the next business day and sends nothing on Saturday: Friday, Saturday and Sunday sales arrive on Monday, or Tuesday after a bank holiday. Instant transfers cost 1.95% of every dollar moved.

ruleCards.title: Disputed card payments
ruleCards.text: When a customer disputes a charge the processor pulls the money back at once. You get 7 days to answer and the bank can take up to 90 days to decide. Square charges no dispute fee, but if you lose, the processing fee is not returned.

ruleCards.title: Card surcharges
ruleCards.text: In New York you may pass on your real card cost only if the higher card price is posted in dollars before the sale. A surprise fee line on the receipt costs up to $500 per violation (General Business Law §518).

ruleCards.title: Fees on top of menu prices
ruleCards.text: A New York City restaurant may not add a surcharge to its listed prices: no "living wage fee", no "admin charge". A real service charge, such as a tip for parties of eight or more, must be disclosed before the customer orders.

ruleCards.title: What an SBA loan asks of you
ruleCards.text: An SBA 7(a) loan needs about 10% of the project in your own cash and a personal guarantee from every owner of 20% or more. Since March 1, 2026 every owner must be a U.S. citizen. Up to $250,000 the rate may reach prime + 6%: 13% today.

ruleCards.title: The SBA guaranty fee
ruleCards.text: From October 2026 the SBA charges 2% of the guaranteed part of loans up to $150,000 and 3% up to $700,000, and lenders pass it on. On a $100,000 loan guaranteed at 85% that is $1,700 before you buy a single cup.

ruleCards.title: Merchant cash advance
ruleCards.text: A cash advance is not a loan: you sell future card sales. $40,000 today for $54,000 taken as 15% of each day's card sales works out near 90% a year. New York makes funders disclose the APR in writing; read it before signing.

ruleCards.title: Personal guarantee
ruleCards.text: A personal guarantee puts your own savings behind the business. An SBA lender must also take a lien on your home if you own 25% or more of its value and the business assets do not fully cover the loan.

ruleCards.title: Good guy guarantee
ruleCards.text: Under a "good guy" guarantee you personally owe the rent only until you hand back the keys: notice given, rent paid, space empty and clean. New York's top court confirmed in 2025 that liability stops on the day you leave.

ruleCards.title: Walking away from a lease
ruleCards.text: A New York commercial landlord has no duty to look for a new tenant after you leave (Holy Properties v. Kenneth Cole, 1995). The space can stay empty while the rent for the rest of the lease is billed to you and your guarantor.

ruleCards.title: What a coffee shop sells for
ruleCards.text: Coffee shops sell for about 2 times the owner's yearly earnings, or 41 cents per dollar of yearly sales (BizBuySell: 1,013 sales, 2021-2025). The median shop sold for $150,000 after 150 days on the market.

ruleCards.title: Selling the shop: the tax department comes first
ruleCards.text: A buyer must notify the state at least 10 days before paying. If the seller owes sales tax, the state claims it from the price. The seller must also collect 8.875% sales tax on the equipment and furniture sold.

ruleCards.title: Your lease after you sell
ruleCards.text: Selling the shop does not end your lease. Unless the landlord signs a written release, the seller and the seller's guarantor stay liable for the rent if the buyer stops paying. Negotiate the release before you sign the lease.

ruleCards.title: What bankruptcy does and does not erase
ruleCards.text: Bankruptcy can erase personally guaranteed rent and loans, but not sales tax you collected or payroll tax you withheld. Filing Chapter 7 costs $338. In New York City up to $204,825 of equity in your home is protected.

ruleCards.title: Wages and the LLC
ruleCards.text: In New York the ten largest owners of an LLC are personally liable for unpaid wages (LLC Law §609(c)). Close the shop owing a final payroll and the staff can collect it from you after giving written notice within 180 days.

ruleCards.title: What the basic policy leaves out
ruleCards.text: A standard business policy does not pay for a flood, a sewer backup, or a power cut that starts outside your shop and the milk that spoils in it. Lost income is covered only after a 72-hour wait. Each gap is a separate add-on.

ruleCards.title: Insurance is billed twice
ruleCards.text: Premiums start as estimates. After the policy year the insurer audits your real payroll for workers' comp and your real sales for liability. Grow faster than you guessed and a bill for the difference arrives.

ruleCards.title: The S corporation in New York City
ruleCards.text: The S corporation saves less here than online advice says. New York City does not recognize it and taxes its profit at 8.85%, against 4% for an LLC, where a credit erases the tax on profit under about $100,000.

ruleCards.title: Weekly pay
ruleCards.text: Counter staff count as manual workers, and New York requires paying them every week (Labor Law §191). Since 2025 a first violation costs interest on the late wages; a repeat costs damages equal to all the wages paid late.

ruleCards.title: Closing has paperwork
ruleCards.text: To close: a final sales tax return within 20 days, a final state payroll return within 30 days of the last wages, final federal returns and W-2s, and $60 to dissolve the LLC. Skip it and penalties grow on a business that is gone.

ruleCards.title: Forgiven debt is income
ruleCards.text: If a lender forgives $20,000 you could not repay, the IRS counts $20,000 as your income (Form 1099-C), unless you were insolvent at that moment or the debt was wiped out in bankruptcy.

ruleCards.title: Your own health insurance
ruleCards.text: Leave your job and its health plan goes too. In 2026 the cheapest silver plan on New York's marketplace costs $807 a month for one adult in Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx, before any subsidy.

ruleCards.title: Gift card money
ruleCards.text: Money from a gift card is not earned until the card is used. In New York a balance left untouched for five years must be handed to the State Comptroller's unclaimed funds office, and cards sold since 2022 may not expire or lose value to fees.

ruleCards.title: The credit for tax on tips
ruleCards.text: You pay 7.65% payroll tax on the tips your staff report. Form 8846 gives it back as a credit against your income tax when their wage is $5.15 an hour or more. On $2,000 of monthly tips that is $153 a month. Many owners never claim it.

ruleCards.title: A city return even when you owe nothing
ruleCards.text: An unincorporated business in New York City with gross income over $95,000 must file an Unincorporated Business Tax return even when the credit wipes the tax out. A cafe passes $95,000 of sales in its second month.

ruleCards.title: Utility deposit
ruleCards.text: Con Edison may ask a new business for a deposit of up to twice its average monthly bill. The money comes back when the account is closed with nothing owed.

ruleCards.title: The city loan fund
ruleCards.text: NYC Future Fund lends $25,000-$500,000 at 7.5% for up to five years with a 3% fee, but only to businesses with 12 months of history and a filed tax return. It can refinance an expensive loan in year two; it cannot fund your opening.

ruleCards.title: Profit is taxed at your family's rate
ruleCards.text: A single-member LLC's profit lands on your personal return on top of a spouse's salary, so each extra dollar is taxed at the household's top rate plus 14.1% self-employment tax. A first-year loss works the other way and cuts the family's tax.

ruleCards.title: Shortages are the owner's loss
ruleCards.text: A short cash drawer, a broken grinder or a customer who walked out may not be taken from wages in New York, not even by asking the worker to pay it back separately (Labor Law §193). Deducted money is owed back double.

ruleCards.title: Disability and Paid Family Leave policy
ruleCards.text: From the first employee New York requires a disability and Paid Family Leave policy. Workers fund most of it: 0.432% of pay in 2026. Going without is a misdemeanor, with a penalty of up to 0.5% of payroll plus $500.

ruleCards.title: Unemployment tax hits early in the year
ruleCards.text: New York unemployment tax is 4.1% on the first $17,600 of each worker's pay and federal tax 0.6% on the first $7,000. So the cost falls in the first months of the year or of a new hire, then stops, and starts again in January.

ruleCards.title: Hidden sales cannot be sold or borrowed against
ruleCards.text: A buyer's bank and an SBA lender value your shop from tax returns. Cash that never reached the books earns no loan and no sale price: at 2 times earnings, each hidden $10,000 of yearly profit cuts about $20,000 off the price.

roadmap.title: Add up where the money will come from
roadmap.text: Most shops open on the owner's savings and family money. An SBA loan wants about 10% of the whole project in your own cash, a personal guarantee and, since March 2026, U.S. citizenship for every owner. Keep three months of fixed costs untouched: lenders will not fund your losses.

roadmap.title: Apply for the loan before you sign the lease
roadmap.text: Ask two or three SBA lenders and one nonprofit microlender. A 7(a) loan up to $250,000 may cost prime + 6% (13% in November 2026) plus a 2% guaranty fee; a microloan gives up to $50,000 at 8%-13% for six years. Make the lease conditional on financing if the landlord will allow it.

roadmap.title: Negotiate your way out before you sign
roadmap.text: Three clauses decide what failure costs: a good guy guarantee instead of a full personal guarantee, the right to assign the lease to a buyer with a written release of you and your guarantor, and a renewal option long enough for a buyer's bank. The city offers free lease review.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Small Business Services (free commercial lease help)

roadmap.title: Open a second account for tax money
roadmap.text: Sales tax (8.875% on top of every sale) and the taxes withheld from pay are not yours. Sweep them into a separate account every day. The sales tax return is due March 20, June 20, September 20 and December 20; payroll deposits on the 15th of each month.
roadmap.agency: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance; IRS

roadmap.title: Read the insurance clause and get quotes
roadmap.text: The lease lists the limits the landlord demands and asks to be named on the policy. Ask the broker what is left out: flood, sewer backup, off-site power failure, spoilage, employee claims. Give honest sales and payroll estimates: the insurer audits both after the year ends.
roadmap.agency: An independent insurance broker; NYS Insurance Fund for workers' compensation

suppliers.what: Banks and licensed lenders that make SBA-guaranteed 7(a) loans for build-out, equipment and working capital
suppliers.whereToFind: SBA Lender Match on sba.gov; ask which local banks made the most small 7(a) loans to restaurants last year. Expect to show a business plan, three years of personal tax returns and the source of your own 10%.
suppliers.examples: Community banks and credit unions with an SBA department
suppliers.note: No lender is named: approval depends on the borrower. Fed survey 2026: 42% of applicants got all they asked for, 22% got nothing; small banks fully approved 57%.

suppliers.what: Loans up to $50,000 at 8%-13% for up to six years, with coaching, for owners banks turn away
suppliers.whereToFind: The SBA's list of microloan intermediaries for New York; community development lenders (CDFIs) in your borough; Kiva for a first $1,000-$15,000 at 0% raised from your own network.
suppliers.note: Seen at SBA: up to $50,000, average about $13,000, generally 8%-13%. Seen at Kiva: 0% interest, no fees, $1,000-$15,000.

suppliers.what: City-backed loans and free one-on-one financing help; the main fund needs 12 months of operating history
suppliers.whereToFind: NYC Business "Financing Assistance" page and the seven NYC Business Solutions Centers; staff match you with lenders at no charge.
suppliers.note: Terms seen on the city page in November 2026; the city says they may change.

suppliers.what: A broker who values the shop, lists it, screens buyers and runs the closing for a commission
suppliers.whereToFind: Listing sites show what similar shops ask; interview brokers who have sold cafes in your borough and ask how many of their listings actually closed.
suppliers.examples: BizBuySell and BizQuest listings; members of the International Business Brokers Association
suppliers.note: Commission: secondary sources give 5%-12% of the price, usually with a minimum; no primary rate card exists. Median time on the market for a coffee shop: 150 days (BizBuySell).

suppliers.what: Auction houses and used dealers that empty a closed shop in days
suppliers.whereToFind: Restaurant auctioneers serving the city, used dealers on the Bowery, and other owners: selling piece by piece takes weeks of paid rent but brings more.
suppliers.examples: Restaurant equipment auction companies; used dealers
suppliers.note: Liquidators say secondary-market value is far below purchase price and everything sells as-is; auction buyers pay a 15%-18% premium on top of the bid. No measured recovery rate was found.

suppliers.category: Trouble: free help before you default
suppliers.what: Free legal and financial counselling for small businesses: lease disputes, debt, closing down
suppliers.whereToFind: NYC Small Business Services (commercial lease assistance and business counsellors); the New York Attorney General's office takes complaints about cash-advance funders.
suppliers.examples: NYC Department of Small Business Services; NY Attorney General
suppliers.note: The Attorney General's 2025 settlement with one cash-advance group cancelled $534 million of merchants' debts.

extra.howNumbersWereChecked: November 14, 2026. The sandbox blocked direct page fetches (sba.gov, tax.ny.gov, irs.gov, squareup.com and others returned a proxy refusal), so every primary source was read through a web search restricted to that source's own domain, which returns the text of the page. verified = the number came back from the primary source's own page that way. estimate = a secondary source, a number carried over from the existing pack, a planning value, or my own arithmetic; the note says which. Game-balance values (demand effects, deductibles, renewal surcharges, days frozen, auction recovery) are design choices and are labelled as such.

eventCatalog.name: Sales tax return due on the 20th
eventCatalog.text: Three months of collected sales tax leave your account in one payment. It was never your money.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYS sales tax quarterly return ST-100, due 20 days after the quarters ending in February, May, August and November

effects.formula: taxable sales of the last three months x 0.08875, minus the vendor credit min(5% of the tax, $200) if paid on time

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Four times a year for every quarterly filer; a new vendor starts as one (TB-ST-275).

eventCatalog.name: Payroll tax deposit on the 15th
eventCatalog.text: Last month's withheld income tax and both halves of Social Security and Medicare are due at the IRS.
eventCatalog.realSignal: IRS monthly deposit schedule: taxes on wages paid in a month are due by the 15th of the next month (Publication 15)

effects.formula: last month's wages x (0.153 + income tax withheld, about 0.08) = about 23% of gross payroll

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every month. A new employer is a monthly depositor for its first calendar year: its lookback period shows zero tax (Publication 15).
eventCatalog.note: On $13,440 of wages plus $2,000 of reported tips: 15.3% x $15,440 = $2,362 of FICA plus roughly $1,200 of withheld income tax. New York withholding is sent separately with Form NYS-1 within five business days of any payroll that brings the unpaid total to $700 (NYS Tax).

eventCatalog.name: Quarterly payroll returns and unemployment tax
eventCatalog.text: Form 941 and the state return NYS-45 are due at the end of the month after each quarter, with the state unemployment tax for the quarter.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYS-45 due April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31 (NYS Tax); Form 941 on the same dates

effects.formula: 4.1% of each worker's wages paid in the quarter until that worker passes $17,600 for the year; federal 0.6% of the first $7,000 once a year in January

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Four times a year. Because of the wage caps the bill is largest for the first quarters of the year and for new hires, then falls to zero.
eventCatalog.note: A barista on $2,940 a month ($21 x 140 h) passes $17,600 in month 6: unemployment tax is $120.54 a month for six months, then nothing until January. Four baristas: about $1,446 for each of the first two quarters. The engine spreads 1.79% evenly; see extra.mechanics.cash_calendar.

eventCatalog.name: Estimated income tax instalment
eventCatalog.text: A quarter of the owner's income tax and self-employment tax for the year is due.
eventCatalog.realSignal: IRS Form 1040-ES due dates for 2026: April 15, June 15, September 15, January 15, 2027; New York follows the same dates

effects.formula: owner taxes accrued since the previous instalment (about 31% of profit in the pack)

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Four times a year for every owner with profit; the periods are uneven: 3, 2, 3 and 4 months.
eventCatalog.note: The engine pays owner taxes on day 20 of the month after each calendar quarter; real dates are the 15th of months 4, 6, 9 and 1. The reference owner accrues $3,026 a month, so the September instalment covers three months ($9,078) and the June one only two ($6,052).

eventCatalog.name: April 15: last year's balance and this year's first instalment
eventCatalog.text: Whatever was not paid for last year is due on the same day as the first instalment for this year.
eventCatalog.realSignal: April 15 filing deadline for Form 1040, NYS IT-201 and NYC-202, and the first 1040-ES instalment

effects.formula: unpaid owner tax for last year + first instalment for this year; + 7% a year interest on last year's short instalments

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Once a year; hits hardest in the first April after the first profitable year, when the safe harbor let the owner pay nothing during the year.
eventCatalog.note: With pay_in_april the reference owner faces $36,300 for last year plus $9,078 for the first quarter on the same day: $45,378, almost a month of sales.

eventCatalog.name: A month with five paydays
eventCatalog.text: Staff are paid every Friday. This month has five Fridays, and rent is the same as always.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Calendar: months with five Fridays (2026: January, May, July, October; 2027: January, April, July, October, December)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Four or five months every year for any employer on the weekly payroll New York requires for manual workers.
eventCatalog.note: Weekly pay is 52 paydays a year, 4.33 a month on average. A five-Friday month costs 5 / 4.33 = 1.154 x the average payroll in cash and a four-Friday month 0.923 x; the year is unchanged. On $13,440: $15,510 against $12,410. Fridays counted by me from the calendar.

eventCatalog.name: Bank holiday: four days of card sales arrive on Tuesday
eventCatalog.text: Monday is a bank holiday. Everything sold by card since Friday morning is still in transit.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Federal Reserve bank holidays that fall on a Monday: Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day

effects.note: about 13% of a month's card sales

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Five Monday holidays a year; a normal weekend already holds three days of sales until Monday.
eventCatalog.note: Square: no standard transfers on Saturday; Friday's balance arrives Monday, or Tuesday if Monday is a bank holiday. 4 days / 30 x $51,000 x 90% on cards x 1.089 = about $6,660 not yet in the bank on the 1st if rent day follows a holiday weekend.

eventCatalog.name: January: every bill at once
eventCatalog.text: The December 20 sales tax return has just gone out. January 15 brings the owner's tax instalment, January 31 the payroll returns, and unemployment tax starts again from zero.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Overlap of the December 20 sales tax date, January 15 estimated tax, January 31 Forms 941/940/NYS-45/W-2 and the reset of the unemployment tax wage bases on January 1

effects.formula: estimated tax for September-December (four months) + first full-rate unemployment tax + federal unemployment tax for the year

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every January. The fourth instalment covers four months, the longest period of the year.
eventCatalog.note: Reference owner: 4 x $3,026 = $12,104 on January 15, a five-Friday payroll in both 2026 and 2027, and $42 x 4 of federal unemployment tax. Demand is also at its yearly low after the holidays (demand numbers belong to D06/D07).

eventCatalog.name: Insurance premium audit
eventCatalog.text: A year after the policy started the insurer asks for your payroll returns and sales reports and recalculates the premium.
eventCatalog.monthsRule: month 13 after the policy starts, then yearly
eventCatalog.realSignal: Policy anniversary: workers' compensation is audited on actual payroll, general liability on actual gross sales

effects.formula: premium x (actual payroll or sales / estimate given at the start - 1), if positive; a refund if negative

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every year for workers' compensation and for sales-rated liability policies.
eventCatalog.note: A shop that told the insurer $400,000 of sales and did $612,000 owes 53% more liability premium for the year in one bill. With the pack's $250 a month that is about $1,590, plus the same percentage on next year's deposit premium.

eventCatalog.name: The Fed moves and so does your loan
eventCatalog.text: The prime rate changes. Variable loans, lines and cards reprice within a month.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Wall Street Journal prime rate (7.00% since September 16, 2026; 6.75% in April-June 2026)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Prime follows each Federal Reserve decision, eight meetings a year; it rose a quarter point once in 2026.
eventCatalog.note: SBA maximums are prime plus a fixed spread, so a variable 7(a) loan moves point for point: +0.25 on $100,000 over ten years is +$14 a month.

eventCatalog.name: Insurers raise rates across the city
eventCatalog.text: Liability and property premiums renew higher for every food business in New York.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Manhattan Chamber of Commerce cost survey of New York-area service firms: business insurance +7%, employee health insurance +12.9%, utilities +8.5%, wages +3.4% in a year (October 2026)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Renewal is yearly; the direction has been up for several years. One bar owner reported a fivefold rise in four years.
eventCatalog.note: Secondary report of a business association survey; applied as a citywide average at renewal.

eventCatalog.name: Workers' comp loss costs cut 21.9%
eventCatalog.text: From October 1 the state's benchmark cost of workers' compensation falls. Your premium follows at renewal.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYS DFS approval of the Compensation Insurance Rating Board's loss cost filing, effective October 1 each year (-21.9% in 2026, -13.2% in 2025)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: One filing a year; two large decreases in a row.
eventCatalog.note: The loss cost is not the price: each carrier applies its own multiplier, so the premium falls by less than 21.9%. Game value -15%.

eventCatalog.name: Your card processor changes its prices
eventCatalog.text: An email announces new processing rates in 30 days.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Processor pricing notices; Square moved in-person payments to 2.6% + 15 cents on February 25, 2025
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every year or two per processor.
eventCatalog.note: Five cents per tap on 5,400 card orders a month is $270 a month.

eventCatalog.name: Court strikes down the cap on debit card fees
eventCatalog.text: An appeals court upholds a ruling against the Federal Reserve's debit fee rule. Banks and merchants wait for a new one.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Eighth Circuit decision of October-November 2026 affirming the vacatur of Regulation II (Corner Post v. Federal Reserve); the cap of 21 cents + 0.05% stays in effect for now
eventCatalog.realFrequency: A once-in-a-decade rule change; its direction is still open.
eventCatalog.note: A flat-rate processor passes nothing through, so the game effect is 1.0 today. The 21 cents fixed part of regulated debit is already 2.5% of an $8.50 ticket, which is why small-ticket shops gain little from interchange-plus pricing.

eventCatalog.name: A wave of closures across the city
eventCatalog.text: More restaurants closed this year than in any year on record. Used equipment is cheap, second-hand spaces are plentiful, and buyers offer less for a running shop.
eventCatalog.realSignal: BLS count of eating and drinking places in New York State: 50,856 in Q1 2025, 48,928 in Q1 2026, the sharpest drop in 36 years of data
eventCatalog.realFrequency: The 2026 drop of 1,928 places (3.8%) was larger than the worst quarter of the pandemic.
eventCatalog.note: The two multipliers are game-balance values. Direction from BizBuySell: the average earnings multiple for coffee shops slipped from 2.35 in 2024 to 2.23 in 2025 (-5%).

eventCatalog.name: New SBA lending rules
eventCatalog.text: The SBA changes who may borrow and what the loan costs.
eventCatalog.realSignal: SBA policy notices: citizenship requirement from March 1, 2026 (microloans from April 1); SOP 50 10 8.1 and the fiscal 2027 fee schedule from October 1, 2026

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Fees are reset every October 1; in fiscal 2025 about 4% of approvals (3,358 of roughly 85,000) went to businesses partly owned by permanent residents.
eventCatalog.note: For a player this is a property of the founder chosen at the start, not a monthly shock.

eventCatalog.name: You now qualify for the city loan fund
eventCatalog.text: Twelve months in business and one filed tax return: the city fund will lend at 7.5%.
eventCatalog.monthsRule: month 13 after opening, once a tax return is filed
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYC Future Fund eligibility: 12 months in business, a filed return, $50,000 of yearly revenue

effects.formula: refinance up to $500,000 at 7.5%, interest-only in weak months, 3% origination fee

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Relaunched in March 2026 with $80 million; the rate was cut from 9% to 7.5%.
eventCatalog.note: Replacing a $40,000 cash advance at about 88% a year with this loan cuts the monthly burden from $6,885 to $250 of interest; the fund still asks for a personal guaranty.

eventCatalog.name: Albany votes on a $17.60 minimum wage
eventCatalog.text: The January increase was cancelled by the law's off-ramp. A bill would raise the floor from March 1.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYS Governor's 2027 minimum wage page: $17.00 stays on January 1, 2027; $17.60 proposed for March 1, 2027, subject to legislation

eventCatalog.text: The marketplace posts next year's premiums. You choose again by the end of January.

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Once a year.
eventCatalog.note: 806.61 / 828.79 = 0.973: the benchmark fell 2.7% for 2026 while employer plans rose. The owner feels whichever one the household is on.

eventCatalog.name: The bank turns the loan down
eventCatalog.text: No operating history, thin collateral: the bank declines. The microlender and your family are still options.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:apply for a bank or SBA loan with less than 10% of the project in own cash, or as a non-citizen
eventCatalog.realSignal: Fed Small Business Credit Survey 2026: 42% of applicants received all the financing they sought, 36% part, 22% none; small banks fully approved 57%

effects.formula: SBA 7(a) is offered only if own cash >= 10% of total project cost and every owner is a citizen

eventCatalog.realFrequency: About one applicant in five gets nothing; restaurants and start-ups are at the weak end.
eventCatalog.note: Deterministic rule for the game, real frequency for the player's plan.

eventCatalog.text: With the bank balance under two weeks of costs, funders start calling. No collateral, no waiting: $40,000 now for $54,000 of future card sales.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:cash falls below two weeks of fixed costs
eventCatalog.realSignal: Fed survey: the share of applicants turning to online lenders rose from 17% (2020) to 29% (2025); 60% of their borrowers found the cost higher than expected

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Offers arrive within days of a public tax warrant or a thin bank balance.
eventCatalog.note: Product terms in extra.financing.merchant_cash_advance.

eventCatalog.text: The daily debits leave too little for rent. Another funder offers to "consolidate".
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:took a cash advance and sales fell or stayed flat
eventCatalog.realSignal: Bloomberg Law: merchant cash advances are piling up in small business bankruptcies; a New York City restaurant group filed in 2026 in a dispute with its cash-advance funders

effects.formula: two holdbacks at once: about 27% of sales

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Stacking is the usual road from one advance to insolvency.

eventCatalog.text: You stopped the daily debits. The funder sends a lien notice to your card processor and sues you personally on the guaranty.
eventCatalog.realSignal: New York Attorney General v. Yellowstone Capital: a $1.065 billion judgment in 2025 over advances collected by fixed daily debits over 60-90 days
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Routine collection practice; the settlement cancelled $534 million of merchants' debts to one group.

eventCatalog.text: Twelve months after opening, the balance on the business card starts to cost about 21% a year.

eventCatalog.monthsRule: month 13 after the card was opened
eventCatalog.realSignal: Issuer terms: 0% introductory periods of about 12 months, then 16.99%-28.74% (NerdWallet, November 2026)

effects.formula: balance x 21% / 12 each month

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Certain for anyone still carrying the balance.
eventCatalog.note: $20,000 carried: $350 a month of interest and a personal credit score that makes the next loan dearer.

eventCatalog.name: Your accountant asks about the family loan

eventCatalog.trigger: decision:borrowed more than $10,000 from family with no written note
eventCatalog.realSignal: IRS applicable federal rates: short-term 4.67% in November 2026 (Rev. Rul. 2026-21)

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Comes up at the first tax return.

eventCatalog.name: The retirement account is now the shop
eventCatalog.text: You funded the opening by rolling your 401(k) into the company. There is no loan payment, and no retirement if the shop fails.
eventCatalog.realSignal: IRS ROBS compliance project: most of the businesses reviewed "either failed or were on the road to failure", with high rates of business and personal bankruptcy

eventCatalog.name: First tax return: most of the opening costs are not deductible yet
eventCatalog.text: Rent and wages paid before opening day come back over 15 years, not this year.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:months of rent and payroll before opening
eventCatalog.realSignal: Internal Revenue Code §195: $5,000 deductible in the first year, reduced dollar for dollar above $50,000 of start-up costs; the rest over 180 months

effects.formula: cash profit + pre-opening costs - min(5000, max(0, 55000 - pre-opening costs)) - (remaining costs / 180 x months open)

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every new business; larger the longer the build-out ran.
eventCatalog.note: Three months of $6,000 rent, $7,000 of professional fees and $4,000 of paid training is $29,000 of start-up costs: $5,000 now and $1,600 a year after. A six-month build-out with a longer payroll run-up takes the total past $50,000, where the first-year $5,000 starts to shrink; at $55,000 it is gone. Equipment and the build-out are different: they can be written off at once (section 179, 100% bonus depreciation).

eventCatalog.name: The first profitable year is taxed all at once
eventCatalog.text: Last year was a loss, so no instalments were required this year. The whole bill lands next April.
eventCatalog.realSignal: IRS safe harbor: no penalty if instalments cover 100% of the previous year's tax, which was zero

effects.formula: a full year of owner tax, about 31% of the year's profit

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Typical in year two.

eventCatalog.name: Sales tax audit letter

eventCatalog.note: Deterministic in the game: an audit finds what is there. The estimate covers months the shop did not cheat too, because the ratio is applied to every quarter.

eventCatalog.name: Unpaid tax: warrant, levy, license, padlock
eventCatalog.text: The state stops writing letters and starts taking.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYS Tax collections: tax warrant (public), levy on bank accounts, income execution up to 10% of wages, driver's license suspension at $10,000 after a 60-day notice, seizure
eventCatalog.realFrequency: In June 2026 the state seized a Manhattan restaurant over more than $1 million of unpaid tax; in October 2026 a restaurateur was convicted of felony tax fraud and fined $100,000 for collected sales tax not paid over.

eventCatalog.text: The sales tax return went in on the 21st. The state keeps the vendor credit and adds a penalty.

eventCatalog.text: Taxable sales passed $300,000 in a quarter. From the next quarter the tax is due every month and the vendor credit ends.

eventCatalog.realSignal: TB-ST-275: $300,000 or more of taxable receipts in a quarter; back to quarterly only after four quarters below

eventCatalog.name: Your accountant finds the tip credit

eventCatalog.realSignal: IRS Form 8846: credit for employer Social Security and Medicare tax on tips when cash wages are at least $5.15 an hour

eventCatalog.text: A large keyed-in payment or a run of disputes trips a risk check. Payouts stop while documents are reviewed.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:keyed in a catering payment above $2,000 on a new account, or three disputes in a month
eventCatalog.realSignal: Processor risk reviews; complaints on record describe accounts closed and balances held for 90 days
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Uncommon and anecdotal (consumer complaint boards, a 2015 NPR report); no rate is published.
eventCatalog.note: The 14 days is a game value; real holds run from two days to 90. Instant transfers lower the balance at risk; an invoice paid by bank transfer avoids the trigger.

eventCatalog.text: The processor pulls $600 back out of your account today. You have seven days to send the signed order.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:takes online, keyed or invoice payments
eventCatalog.realSignal: Square: disputed funds held at once, 7 days to respond, up to 90 days for the bank to decide, no dispute fee, processing fee lost if the customer wins
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Rare for tapped cards at a counter; mostly keyed and online payments.
eventCatalog.note: Budgeted in the monthly cost refunds_and_disputes.

eventCatalog.name: A customer falls and files a claim
eventCatalog.text: The insurer takes over the claim. You pay the deductible now and a higher premium at renewal.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:wet floor, icy entrance or broken step left unfixed (see D07, D08)
eventCatalog.realSignal: The Hartford, 2020-2024 small-business claims: customer injuries and slips are about 20% of claims, double their share ten years earlier
eventCatalog.realFrequency: The Hartford (2015): four in ten small businesses have a property or liability claim within ten years.
eventCatalog.note: Deductible and the 15% renewal surcharge are game values; no public table. New York City puts sidewalk liability on the property owner (Administrative Code §7-210) and the lease passes the cost to the tenant through indemnity and insurance clauses.

eventCatalog.name: Break-ins on your block
eventCatalog.text: Several storefronts were broken into overnight. A smashed door, an empty till, a missing tablet.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYPD CompStat burglary counts for the precinct; The Hartford: burglary and theft are about 20% of small-business claims, $8,000 on average in its 2015 study
eventCatalog.realFrequency: One of the two most common small-business claims.
eventCatalog.note: Announced for the whole block, so it is not a dice roll: every shop takes the hit and the insured ones pay only the deductible. Cash in the till is usually covered only up to a small sublimit.

eventCatalog.name: A pipe bursts in the apartment above
eventCatalog.text: Water comes through the ceiling over the bar. Two weeks closed for repairs.
eventCatalog.realSignal: The Hartford: water and freezing damage is the most common small-business claim, 20-22% of claims, $34,600 on average (2020-2024)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: The single most frequent property claim; winter cold snaps cluster them.
eventCatalog.note: Business income cover starts after a 72-hour wait, so the first three days of lost sales are the owner's. Announce it with the cold-snap event of D07.

eventCatalog.name: The claim for spoiled milk is denied
eventCatalog.text: A neighbourhood power cut spoiled the fridge. The basic policy excludes failures that start outside your premises.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Con Edison outage (events of D03/D07); standard policies exclude off-premises utility failure unless a utility services endorsement and a spoilage endorsement are bought

effects.formula: value of chilled stock, about $600, plus lost sales, unless insurance_package >= plus_breakdown

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Summer peak days.
eventCatalog.note: Stock value is a planning figure: a week of milk and pastry.

eventCatalog.name: The drain backs up and the policy says no
eventCatalog.text: Grease and coffee grounds block the line and the floor floods. Sewer backup is an exclusion unless you bought the add-on.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:skip_grease_trap_cleaning for three months or more
eventCatalog.realSignal: Grease interceptor more than 25% full (existing violation grease_interceptor_neglect)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: A standard exclusion.
eventCatalog.note: Links an existing shortcut to an insurance consequence.

eventCatalog.name: A former barista sues
eventCatalog.text: The complaint claims unpaid wages and wrongful firing. The liability policy does not cover employment claims.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:any labor shortcut found, or a firing during a complaint
eventCatalog.realSignal: Labor Law §198: wages owed back double for up to six years; LLC Law §609(c): the ten largest members of an LLC are personally liable for unpaid wages

effects.formula: legal defense, about $10,000 as a game value (the average EPLI deductible), plus what the labor violation itself costs

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Wage claims are the most common suit against New York restaurants.
eventCatalog.note: Employment practices cover answers the firing claim; the wage part is usually excluded, so the shortcut is never insured.

eventCatalog.name: A broker brings a buyer
eventCatalog.text: After six profitable months a buyer offers two times your yearly earnings.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:six months in a row of positive reported profit
eventCatalog.realSignal: BizBuySell: sold coffee shops went for a median of 2.00 x owner earnings (middle half 1.50-2.55) and 0.41 x yearly sales (0.30-0.57)
