eventCatalog.note: Replaces the placeholder of 20% of yearly sales in the keen-cray branch (extra.takeover). The reference shop: $116,600 of yearly owner earnings x 2.0 = $233,000, or 0.38 x its $612,000 of sales.

eventCatalog.name: The buyer's bank reads your tax returns
eventCatalog.text: The price is built on reported profit. Cash that never reached the books is worth nothing to the bank.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:underreport_sales was used in the last 12 months
eventCatalog.realSignal: Lender and buyer due diligence on three years of tax returns

effects.formula: minus 2.0 x hidden yearly profit

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Standard in every financed sale.
eventCatalog.note: Hiding a tenth of $612,000 of sales hides about $61,000 of profit and takes roughly $122,000 off the price: far more than the $18,000 a year it saved.

eventCatalog.name: The landlord will not sign the assignment
eventCatalog.text: The buyer needs your lease. The landlord asks for a fee and a higher rent, or says no.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:selling with no assignment clause, or fewer than five years left on the lease
eventCatalog.realSignal: Lease assignment clause and remaining term; New York listings state the years left (one Queens cafe: three years)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: The most common reason a small restaurant sale dies.
eventCatalog.note: The halving is a game value: a shop that cannot hand over its lease sells for its equipment. Fixed at lease signing by the roadmap step negotiate_exit_terms.

eventCatalog.name: The buyer stops paying rent and the landlord calls you
eventCatalog.text: You sold the shop a year ago. The lease was assigned without a release.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:sold with an assignment and no written release
eventCatalog.realSignal: New York law: an assignor stays liable on the lease unless the landlord expressly releases it

effects.formula: rent for the months the buyer misses, until the space is surrendered

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Happens whenever the buyer fails; one in five new food places closes in its first year.
eventCatalog.note: In a 12-month season this matters as a line in the final plan the player takes into real life.

eventCatalog.name: Auction day
eventCatalog.text: Everything in the shop is sold as-is in one afternoon.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Auctioneers: secondary-market value is far below purchase price; buyers pay a 15-18% premium on top of the bid

effects.formula: 25% of what the equipment and furniture cost new, minus 15% commission; build-out: nothing

eventCatalog.realFrequency: No measured recovery rate was found; 25% is a planning value.
eventCatalog.note: Standard kit: about $36,500 of equipment and furniture brings roughly $7,800 after commission; the $70,000 build-out stays with the landlord. Sales tax must be collected from the buyers.

eventCatalog.name: The landlord keeps part of the deposit
eventCatalog.text: Unpaid rent and the cost of restoring the space come out of the security deposit.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:close the business with rent owed or the space not restored
eventCatalog.realSignal: Lease surrender terms: rent paid to the surrender date, space empty and broom-clean

effects.formula: deposit minus arrears minus restoration

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Usual when a shop closes in arrears.
eventCatalog.note: Leaving clean and paid up under a good guy guarantee returns the three-month deposit ($18,000) and ends personal liability on that day.

eventCatalog.name: A tax bill addressed to you personally
eventCatalog.text: Months after the shop closed, the state assesses its unpaid sales tax against you as a responsible person.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:closed with unpaid sales tax or withheld payroll tax
eventCatalog.realSignal: Tax Law §1133 (responsible persons); Trust Fund Recovery Penalty; neither is erased by Chapter 7

effects.formula: all unpaid trust taxes + penalties + interest; collected by income execution of up to 10% of gross wages at the next job

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Automatic: the state files against responsible persons when a business closes owing tax.
eventCatalog.note: Order of payment on the way out matters: trust taxes first, wages second, everyone else after.

eventCatalog.name: Chapter 7
eventCatalog.text: The guaranteed lease, the loan and the cards are more than you own. Bankruptcy wipes them out and leaves the tax debts.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:closed with personally guaranteed debts larger than non-exempt assets
eventCatalog.realSignal: U.S. Bankruptcy Court fee schedule: Chapter 7 $338, Chapter 13 $313, Chapter 11 $1,738; New York homestead exemption $204,825 in the city for April 2024 - March 2027

effects.formula: guaranteed rent, loans and cards go to zero; trust taxes stay; home equity above $204,825 is at risk

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Subchapter V, the small-business reorganization, takes debts up to $3,424,000.
eventCatalog.note: For the final report of a failed game: what the player would still owe in real life.

eventCatalog.name: Form 1099-C arrives
eventCatalog.text: A lender settled for less. The forgiven part is reported to the IRS as your income.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:settled a debt for less than owed while still solvent
eventCatalog.realSignal: IRS Publication 4681: canceled debt is ordinary income unless the borrower was insolvent or in bankruptcy

effects.formula: + forgiven amount, unless liabilities exceeded assets just before

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every settlement of $600 or more is reported.
eventCatalog.note: Most owners who settle are insolvent and owe nothing; the form still has to be answered with Form 982.

eventCatalog.name: Outstanding gift cards
eventCatalog.text: The buyer deducts unredeemed gift cards from the price; in a closure their holders become creditors.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:sold gift cards and then sold or closed the business
eventCatalog.realSignal: Gift card liability on the balance sheet; New York: balances untouched for five years go to the State Comptroller

effects.formula: minus outstanding gift card balance

eventCatalog.realFrequency: The Attorney General recovered $36 million from one retailer that kept unused balances.
eventCatalog.note: Selling gift cards just before a planned closure is fraud, not a cash-flow tool.

eventCatalog.name: Your unemployment tax rate is recalculated
eventCatalog.text: Former staff claimed benefits. The state charges them to your account and sets your own rate.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:laid off or fired workers who then claimed unemployment benefits
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYS DOL experience rating: new employers pay 4.1%; rated employers paid between 1.7% and 9.5% in 2026

effects.formula: rate moves from 4.1% toward 9.5% of the first $17,600 per worker: up to +$950 per worker a year

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Rates are set once a year, in February-March.
eventCatalog.note: (9.5% - 4.1%) x $17,600 = $950. A new employer keeps 4.1% until it has enough quarters of history, so this is a second-year effect.

eventCatalog.name: The household runs out of savings
eventCatalog.text: The shop covers its own bills but not yet yours.
eventCatalog.trigger: decision:owner draw set above profit after tax, with a fixed personal reserve at the start
eventCatalog.realSignal: Household budget: own health insurance $807 a month per adult on the marketplace in 2026

effects.formula: forced down to profit after tax; the gap is new personal debt at about 21%

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Fed survey 2026: 54% of employer firms met a financial challenge with the owner's personal funds.

mechanics.title: Loan: borrowing to open (and to refinance)
mechanics.playerDecision: In the opening plan the player builds the funding: own savings first, then any products from extra.financing that the founder qualifies for, each with an amount; chooses fixed or variable interest (lever loan_rate_type). From month 13 the city fund can replace expensive debt.
mechanics.engineMath: On draw: cash += amount - fees. Each month: payment = P x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n) with r = yearly rate / 12, split into interest (an expense) and principal (not an expense, but cash out). Payments start the month after the draw, so a loan taken at lease signing is serviced through the whole build-out with no sales. Variable loans reprice with event prime_rate_move: rate = prime + spread. Eligibility is a rule, not a roll: SBA 7(a) only if own cash >= 10% of total project cost (all setup items + pre-opening rent + three months of fixed costs) and the founder is a citizen; microloan capped at $50,000; city fund only after 12 months and a filed return. Every product has a personalGuarantee flag: on closure the unpaid balance of flagged debt becomes the owner's personal debt (mechanic exit_closure). Three missed payments call the loan. Net worth for the leaderboard = cash + resale value of assets - all debt.

mechanics.title: Cash advance: fast money against future card sales
mechanics.playerDecision: When cash falls under two weeks of fixed costs the event cash_advance_calls offers $40,000 for $54,000. The player accepts, declines, or uses bill_timing first. A second advance can be stacked on the first.
mechanics.engineMath: On accept: cash += 40000 (less a 2% origination fee as a game value); liability 54000. Each day: min(remaining, 0.15 x card sales of the day) leaves cash, card sales being 90% of sales. Nothing is "interest": the whole $14,000 difference is a financing cost spread over the days of collection. Show the player the yearly rate before signing, as New York law requires the funder to: with flat sales it is about 88% nominal, 134% effective. If sales fall the advance lasts longer and the rate falls, but a fixed daily debit version does not adjust. Stopping payment triggers advance_default_freeze and puts the balance into the owner's personal debt when guaranteed.

mechanics.title: Payment calendar: profit is not cash
mechanics.playerDecision: None directly: the player sees a 60-day cash forecast with every dated payment, and chooses a cushion, the tax reserve lever, payout speed and who waits when the cushion is gone.
mechanics.engineMath: Keep a daily cash ledger separate from the monthly profit-and-loss statement. Inflows: cash sales the same day; card sales with a lag (next business day, none on Saturday, bank holidays skipped). Outflows on their real days from extra.paymentCalendar: rent day 1; wages every Friday; federal payroll deposit on the 15th; sales tax on the 20th of months 3, 6, 9, 12; payroll returns at the end of months 1, 4, 7, 10; owner tax on the 15th of months 4, 6, 9, 1. Unemployment taxes accrue at the statutory rate until each worker's wage base is reached (4.1% to $17,600; 0.6% to $7,000), not at a flat share. A day that ends below zero triggers, in order: late rent fee, supplier hold, missed tax deposit (a violation), missed payroll (a wage claim). The month can show a profit while the 20th shows an overdraft.

mechanics.title: Taxable profit is not cash profit
mechanics.playerDecision: Indirect: how long the build-out runs before opening, and whether equipment is bought (written off at once) or leased.
mechanics.engineMath: Keep a tax ledger beside the cash ledger. Start-up costs = everything spent before opening day except equipment, build-out and deposits (rent, wages, training, professional fees, utilities). Deduct min(5000, max(0, 55000 - startupCosts)) in the opening year and the rest at 1/180 a month. Equipment and the build-out (interior improvements to a leased shop) may be written off in the opening year under section 179 or 100% bonus depreciation; the engine can take them in full against that year's profit and carry the unused loss forward. So a shop that broke even in cash can owe tax (start-up costs capitalised) or owe none despite cash profit (equipment written off). At sale, written-off equipment comes back as ordinary income.

mechanics.title: What the state does about unpaid tax, step by step
mechanics.playerDecision: After keep_sales_tax or spend_payroll_withholding: pay in full, ask for an instalment agreement, or keep not paying.
mechanics.engineMath: Months unpaid 1-2: penalty and interest accrue (10% + 1% a month to 30% on sales tax; 2%-15% on federal deposits; interest daily). Month 3: bill and notice; the debt becomes visible to officials who take the case. Month 6: tax warrant, a public lien: lenders refuse new credit and cash-advance funders start calling. Month 9: levy: the bank account is frozen for 10 days and the balance taken up to the debt. At $10,000 of state debt: 60-day notice, then license suspension (a reputation hit in the game). Month 12: seizure: the shop is closed. An instalment agreement (debt / 24 a month as a game value) freezes the ladder while every payment is made; two misses in twelve months restart it at the levy. The debt never leaves the owner.

mechanics.title: Exit: selling the business
mechanics.playerDecision: From month 7 the player may list the shop. Choices: asking price, broker or not, cash only or a seller note, and whether the lease can be assigned (decided back at signing).
mechanics.engineMath: Value = 2.0 x reported owner earnings of the last 12 months (owner's own pay added back), bounded by 0.30-0.57 x yearly sales; hidden sales do not count. A shop with no profit sells only its assets and lease: second-hand value of equipment plus whatever a buyer saves on build-out. Time to close: 150 days of game time during which sales must hold; a letter grade below A or a visible violation cuts the multiple to the low quartile (1.5). Deductions at closing: broker 10%; loan balances; the state's claim for unpaid sales tax (bulk sale rule: the buyer notifies the state 10 days ahead and holds the price until cleared); income tax on the gain at 28%. The buyer pays 8.875% sales tax on the equipment part. The Health Department permit does not transfer. If the lease has no assignment right the price is halved. If the landlord did not release the seller, the lease liability stays with the seller for the rest of the term. This replaces the fixed rule in the keen-cray branch (20% of yearly sales, $80,000-$200,000) for both buying and selling: one formula, seen from two sides.

mechanics.title: Exit: closing down, and what follows the owner home
mechanics.playerDecision: Close now or keep going; surrender the space properly (notice, rent paid, empty) or walk away; sell equipment piece by piece over two more months of rent or at auction now; which debts to pay with the last cash.
mechanics.engineMath: Closing sequence. (1) Last cash is applied in the order the player chooses; the advisor recommends trust taxes, then wages, then secured lenders, then everyone else, because the first two follow the owner personally (sales tax: Tax Law §1133; withheld payroll tax: Trust Fund Recovery Penalty; wages: LLC Law §609(c)) and are not erased by bankruptcy. (2) Equipment and furniture: 25% of cost new at auction less 15% commission, or 40% over two months of private sales (both game values); a lender with a lien takes the proceeds first. The build-out is worth nothing. (3) Lease: with a good guy guarantee liability stops on the day the keys go back, if notice was given and rent is paid; the deposit comes back less arrears and restoration. With a full guarantee the remaining rent is owed as it falls due and the landlord need not relet. (4) Guaranteed loans, leases and cards become personal debt. (5) Final sales tax return in 20 days, final payroll returns, W-2s, $60 dissolution; unfiled returns keep generating penalties (existing violation returns_not_filed). (6) If personal debt exceeds what the owner has: Chapter 7 for $338 erases the guaranteed debts, not the trust taxes; home equity is protected to $204,825. nonObvious.text: New York sales tax is due on March 20, June 20, September 20 and December 20, not after calendar quarters.
nonObvious.why: A new owner budgets for January, April, July and October and is one month wrong four times a year; December 20 lands five days before Christmas.

nonObvious.text: The state pays you up to $200 a quarter for filing sales tax on time.
nonObvious.why: The vendor collection credit is 5% of the tax, capped at $200; one late day loses it and adds a penalty of at least $50.

nonObvious.text: An LLC does not protect its owner from sales tax, withheld payroll tax or unpaid wages.
nonObvious.why: Three of the debts most likely to exist at closing are exactly the three the law attaches to the person; all three also survive bankruptcy or are collected first.

nonObvious.text: Unemployment taxes are paid almost entirely in the first half of the year.
nonObvious.why: 4.1% applies to the first $17,600 per worker and the federal 0.6% to the first $7,000, so the cost stops mid-year and restarts in January, the weakest month.

nonObvious.text: Weekly pay is the law for counter staff, so four or five months a year have five payrolls.
nonObvious.why: Rent is monthly, wages are weekly: a five-Friday month costs 15% more cash in wages than the average month.

nonObvious.text: Card money taken on Friday morning can arrive on Tuesday.
nonObvious.why: No standard transfers on Saturday and none on bank holidays: a holiday weekend parks about 13% of a month's card sales just as rent falls due.

nonObvious.text: The card processor reports all card sales to the IRS with no minimum.
nonObvious.why: An owner who hides cash is audited from the card total upward: the state watches the register for a day and applies the cash ratio to three years.

nonObvious.text: Money spent before opening is deducted over 15 years, not in year one.
nonObvious.why: Only $5,000 of start-up costs is deductible at once, and nothing once they reach $55,000: long build-outs make taxable profit higher than cash profit.

nonObvious.text: In a first profitable year the IRS safe harbor lets an owner legally pay nothing until April, then everything at once.
nonObvious.why: The rule that removes the penalty also removes the discipline; the April bill is a quarter of the year's profit plus the new year's first instalment.

nonObvious.text: The S corporation saves almost nothing in New York City.
nonObvious.why: The city ignores the election and charges 8.85% on the profit left after salary; at $117,000 of profit the saving is about $3,000 before the extra accounting costs.

nonObvious.text: A city business tax return is due even when no city business tax is due.
nonObvious.why: UBT must be filed above $95,000 of gross income; the credit erases the tax until profit reaches about $100,000.

nonObvious.text: The profit of the shop is taxed at the family's top rate.
nonObvious.why: With a spouse earning $90,000 the same $117,000 of profit pays 21% income tax instead of 17%; a first-year loss gives 20 cents on the dollar back.

nonObvious.text: The payroll tax paid on staff tips comes back as a credit.
nonObvious.why: Form 8846 returns 7.65% of reported tips; an owner without an accountant never sees it.

nonObvious.text: Since March 2026 a green card is not enough for an SBA loan.
nonObvious.why: Every owner must be a U.S. citizen or national; about 4% of the loans approved the year before had permanent-resident owners.

nonObvious.text: The city's cheap loan fund cannot be used to open.
nonObvious.why: It needs 12 months in business and a filed tax return; it is a year-two refinancing tool.

nonObvious.text: A loan is repaid from the month after it is drawn, sales or no sales.
nonObvious.why: A $100,000 SBA loan costs $1,493 a month through the whole build-out, on top of the rent the user already called "a pure minus".

nonObvious.text: An SBA lender may take a lien on the owner's home.
nonObvious.why: Required when the loan is not fully secured and the owner has 25% or more equity in the property.

nonObvious.text: A cash advance is priced as a "factor", which hides a rate near 90% a year.
nonObvious.why: $40,000 for $54,000 sounds like 35%; collected over eight months from daily sales it is about 88%.

nonObvious.text: Surprise card fees are illegal, posted card prices are legal.
nonObvious.why: The difference between a $500 violation and a lawful 3% is a price tag posted before the sale.

nonObvious.text: A New York City cafe may not add any fee on top of menu prices.
nonObvious.why: The "wellness fee" and "admin charge" common elsewhere are violations here unless they are true service charges disclosed before ordering.

nonObvious.text: The basic business policy does not cover the three things most likely to close a cafe for a week.
nonObvious.why: Sewer backup, off-site power failure with spoilage, and flood are exclusions; lost income starts paying after 72 hours.

nonObvious.text: Insurance sends a second bill after the year ends.
nonObvious.why: Liability is rated on sales and workers' comp on payroll; a shop that beat its own forecast pays the difference in one bill.

nonObvious.text: Workers' compensation got cheaper while everything else got dearer.
nonObvious.why: New York cut loss costs 21.9% in October 2026 and 13.2% a year earlier; business insurance overall rose 7%.

nonObvious.text: Leaving a job to open a cafe costs about $800 a month per adult in health insurance.
nonObvious.why: The cheapest silver plan in Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx is $806.61 in 2026; it is not on the shop's books but leaves the same pocket.

nonObvious.text: A coffee shop sells for about two years of its owner's earnings.
nonObvious.why: Median 2.0 x earnings and 0.41 x sales across 1,013 sales; the median price of $150,000 is less than a New York build-out costs.

nonObvious.text: Selling a healthy one-year-old shop at the market multiple does not return the money put in.
nonObvious.why: After the broker, the loan payoff and tax on a price that is nearly all gain, the reference owner keeps about $71,000.

nonObvious.text: Hidden cash sales make the business worth less than it earns.
nonObvious.why: Buyers and their banks value tax returns: each $10,000 of hidden yearly profit removes about $20,000 from the price.

nonObvious.text: After selling the shop the seller can still owe its rent.
nonObvious.why: An assignment leaves the original tenant and guarantor liable unless the landlord signs a release.

nonObvious.text: The kind of guarantee signed on day one decides the cost of failure on the last day.
nonObvious.why: Good guy: liability ends when the keys go back. Full guarantee: nine years of rent with no duty on the landlord to relet.

nonObvious.text: The buyer of a shop pays sales tax on its equipment.
nonObvious.why: 8.875% on furniture and equipment, collected by the seller with the final return; nobody budgets for it.

nonObvious.text: Closing has a 20-day deadline.
nonObvious.why: The final sales tax return is due 20 days after the last day of business; skipping it starts penalties on a dead company.

nonObvious.text: A forgiven debt is taxable income.
nonObvious.why: A settlement with a lender produces Form 1099-C unless the owner was insolvent at that moment.

nonObvious.text: Gift cards sold are a debt, and in five years the state wants what was not spent.
nonObvious.why: New York forbids fees and expiry, and unredeemed balances go to the Comptroller.

nonObvious.text: A register shortage is the owner's loss by law.
nonObvious.why: Deductions for shortages or breakage are illegal even with the worker's consent.

nonObvious.text: Paying every two weeks became survivable in 2025, once.
nonObvious.why: A first frequency-of-pay claim now costs interest; a second one costs damages equal to all wages paid late.

nonObvious.text: Used equipment brings a fraction of its price, and the lender takes it first.
nonObvious.why: Auction buyers pay well under used-dealer prices, and an SBA lender holds a lien on everything the loan bought.

nonObvious.text: More restaurants disappeared in New York in early 2026 than in any quarter of the pandemic.
nonObvious.why: Down 1,928 in a year; for a newcomer that means cheaper used equipment and more second-hand spaces, and for a seller a lower price.

nonObvious.text: Square charges no fee for a dispute but keeps the processing fee on a refund or a lost dispute.
nonObvious.why: The cost of a disputed $600 order is $600 plus about $16.

failureStories.what: A Manhattan restaurant was seized by the state tax department in June 2026.
failureStories.cause: More than $1 million of unpaid tax owed by the restaurant and its owner.
failureStories.lesson: Unpaid trust taxes end with a padlock, and the owner is named with the business.

failureStories.what: A Harlem restaurateur was convicted of felony tax fraud in October 2026 and fined $100,000.
failureStories.cause: Sales tax collected from customers and repeatedly not reported or paid over.
failureStories.lesson: Keeping collected sales tax is prosecuted as a crime, not handled as a late bill.

failureStories.what: A New York City restaurant group with nine restaurants filed for bankruptcy in 2026.
failureStories.cause: Mounting debt and a dispute with its merchant cash advance funders over their claims on its sales.
failureStories.lesson: Cash advances reach even established operators and are the debt they end up fighting in court.

failureStories.what: An Upper West Side cafe closed in April 2026 after 38 years.
failureStories.cause: The owner could no longer afford the rent.
failureStories.lesson: A long record does not protect against the lease renewal.

failureStories.what: A Midtown restaurant open since the 1970s closed in 2026.
failureStories.cause: Its co-owner said the rent had become "very, very expensive".
failureStories.lesson: Rent as a share of sales is the number to watch every year, not only at signing.

failureStories.what: A specialty roaster closed its Williamsburg cafe in September 2026.
failureStories.cause: The lease expired and no way to keep the cafe open was found.
failureStories.lesson: Without a renewal option a profitable shop has an end date, and no sale value in its last two years.

failureStories.what: Thousands of small businesses that took advances from one group of funders had their debts cancelled in 2025.
failureStories.cause: Advances collected by fixed daily debits at rates the Attorney General called illegal loans.
failureStories.lesson: The remedy came years after the businesses needed it; the APR disclosure now required is the protection to use before signing.

failureStories.what: A New York bar owner reported liability insurance up fivefold in four years, to $24,000 a year (2026).
failureStories.cause: Rising liability premiums across the city.
failureStories.lesson: Insurance is not a fixed cost: budget the renewal, and keep claims off the record.
